promptLatex: How many nonnegative integer solutions does x + y + z = 10 have?
hintLatex: This is a stars-and-bars problem. The formula for the number of nonnegative integer solutions to x_1 + ... + x_k = n is \binom{n+k-1}{k-1}.
Here n = 10 and k = 3, so the answer is \binom{10+3-1}{3-1} = \binom{12}{2}.
solutionLatex:
Using stars and bars, the number of nonnegative integer solutions to x + y + z = 10 is \binom{10+3-1}{3-1} = \binom{12}{2}.

\binom{12}{2} = \frac{12 \times 11}{2} = 66.
